nahhas-irab:1-1.t: The alif was dropped from ترى for the jussive. The original has a hamza (ترأى); the vowel of the hamza was cast onto the rāʾ and the hamza was dropped. «كيف» is in the position of the accusative by فعل; it is not declined because it is in the sense of particles, even though it is a noun, and the fāʾ took fatḥa because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: I.e., in frustration of what they intended.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t:
Among the best things narrated about it from the early (scholars) is what ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad, who said: ʿAffān narrated to us, saying: Ḥammād narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim, from Zirr, from ʿAbd Allāh: طَيْراً أَبابِيلَ, he said: (in) groups. And it was read before Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar, from Yūsuf ibn Mūsā, who said: Shihāb narrated to us, from Ibrāhīm, from Ḥumayd, from Abū Khālid, from Abū Ṣāliḥ: «طيرا أبابيل», he said: gathering after gathering.
Abū Jaʿfar said: It is well known in the speech of the Arabs: "they came abābīl", i.e., group after group, a great, numerous group after a group. It is derived from abala ʿalayhi, when it became numerous and gathered; and from this the camels (ibil) were named, because of the greatness of their build. It has been said that the meaning of أَفَلا يَنْظُرُونَ إِلَى الْإِبِلِ كَيْفَ خُلِقَتْ [al-Ghāshiya: 17] is that they are the clouds, because of their greatness, even though al-Qutabī rejected this interpretation without an established proof. The most correct thing said about the singular of al-abābīl is what Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: its singular is ibbīl, like sikkīn and sakākīn.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: The kāf is in the position of the accusative as a second object, i.e., (like straw) whose contents have been eaten — it is the husk of the wheat. It may also be in the sense of "eaten by livestock".
